topics.label: Introduction to the initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines its focus on integrating immune system components to understand inflammatory reactions.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the structure, ligand diversity, cellular localization, and downstream signaling cascades of Toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptors and the inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail intracellular sensing mechanisms, focusing on Nod-like receptors and inflammasome assembly that processes pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Cellular dynamics and physiological outcomes of acute inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sentinel cells coordinate leukocyte recruitment into tissues, fluid drainage, and the systemic consequences of excessive inflammatory signaling.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system actively shuts down acute inflammation, repairs damaged tissue, and manages persistent insults through chronic granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the end of the lecture and previews the topic of the next session.
